Any more elegant solutions out there?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io: Common or unique working directory for each instance of an app?
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io: Common or unique working directory for each instance of an app?
messages.body_plain:
Yes. Each R process (worker) runs in the same directory on the server. A worker process can handle more then one session (connection). Additionally your application will automatically start more then one worker process if its needed (depending on the application settings and the number of connections). If two sessions (connections) need isolation to write files, you should create a temp directory.

If you have more then one instance of the application (e.g. more then one server), all their workers will also be running in the same directory.

-Andy

#server.R

#Get current wd and print
currwd <- getwd()

#FUNCTION - new directory
fn_dir <- function(currwd=NULL)
{
  if(is.null(currwd)) stop("Argument 'currwd' is empty.\n")

  #Create new working directory

  newwd <- paste0(currwd,"/",format(Sys.time(),"%Y%m%d%H%M%S"))
  dir.create(newwd)
  newwd

}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  #REACTIVE - store
  store <- reactiveValues(currwd = currwd)

  #REACTIVE - complete input
  fn_getfilenames <- reactive({
    inputdata <- input$upload

    if (!is.null(inputdata))
    {

      store$newwd <- fn_dir(store$currwd)

      return(inputdata)
    }else{
      return(NULL)
    }
  })

  #OUTPUT
  output$display <- renderPrint({
    if (is.null(fn_getfilenames())) return(NULL)

    inputdata <- fn_getfilenames()

    #some stuff to export to working directory

    rcontent <- as.vector(scan(file = inputdata$datapath,what = "text",n = 10))

    full_file_path <- file.path(store$newwd,inputdata$name)
    write(x = rcontent, file = paste0(full_file_path,"-test.txt"))

    return(str(inputdata))
  })
})

The active hours are measured on the instance level, your 5 minute timeout is applying on the instance level as well.  Let us say you have 10 people hitting your application in an hour for 5 minutes each, but you have only configured one instance (an instance can have more than one R worker process).  Then your account will consume 60 minutes.  It might be helpful to read this article to make sure the notion of instances and workers are clear.  I will add an item to our backlog to do a better job explaining how active hours are tracked.

Tareef

You can do:

deployApp("path/to/my/app", appName="URP-version1")

The other option is delete the rsconnect directory in side your application, and then rename the directory to "URP-version1".

After that you can simply terminate, and then delete the old one.

", "Attributed Physician: ", dataset$docID) popupUC <- paste0("Member ID: ", ucdata$member_id, "
", "Attributed Physician: ", ucdata$docID) ### Plotting the Map proxy <- leafletProxy("map") if (input$view==TRUE & input$crit=="EVH" & input$doc==FALSE && input$census==FALSE) { proxy %>% clearMarkers() %>% clearShapes() %>% clearPopups %>% clearControls %>% store } else if(input$view==TRUE && input$crit=="EVH" && input$doc==TRUE && input$census==FALSE) { proxy %>% clearMarkers() %>% clearShapes() %>% clearControls %>% addCircleMarkers(~longitude, ~latitude, layerId=~member_id, stroke=FALSE, fillOpacity=0.9, fillColor="Red", data=dataset, popup=popupEVH) %>% addCircleMarkers(~longitude, ~latitude, layerId=~docID, fillColor="Green", stroke=FALSE, data=docdata) } else if(input$view==TRUE && input$crit=="EVH" && input$doc==TRUE && input$census==TRUE) { proxy %>% clearMarkers() %>% clearShapes() %>% clearControls %>% addPolygons(data = income_census, fillColor = ~pal(percent), color = "#b2aeae", # you need to use hex colors fillOpacity = 0.4, weight = 1, smoothFactor = 0.2) %>% addLegend(pal = pal, values = income_census$percent, position = "bottomleft", title = "Percent of Households

Any tips?

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Cannot logout of a shinyapps.io app
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Cannot logout of a shinyapps.io app
messages.body_plain:
We've recently changed the way logging into an application hosted on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> works. This was necessary to improve security. It is now a two step process (Both steps are completed in the popup window, when you click 'Login' for a private app):

1) You must first authenticate to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service (login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io>). When you do this, we create a session cookie for login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io> (called shinyapps_auth).

2) Once you've authenticated to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service you can then authenticate to the application itself using your existing session for login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io>. This sets another cookie called (therealshinyapps) for the specific application you are logging into.

As I said, both these steps happen automatically when you click "Login" for a private application. The two login steps are necessary, because these cookies must be distinct between shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> itself, and between applications hosted on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

As Fereshteh mentioned, you can logout of an application by visiting the URL: https://userName.shinyapps.io/appName/__logout__/. When you visit this URL you are in fact logged out the application, but you're still got a session cookie for login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io>, so clicking "Login" will simply authenticate you the application using your existing login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io> session without requiring you to re-enter your password.

Currently the login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io> uses a session cookie so if you close your window it *should* require you to re-authenticate with login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io> the next time you attempt to authenticate to an application. That said, it turns out both Chrome and Firefox keep these session cookies around for longer then they should unless you disable the "feature". See this thread <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/10617954/chrome-doesnt-delete-session-cookies> for more info. Regardless you can always logout of the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service itself by going to https://login.shinyapps.io/logout after you logout of your application. I have some ideas on how to address this, so its something we can likely fix.

I apologize if this is all bit confusing. We've recently done a lot work to improve the security of private applications, and as is typically the case with additional security, it can create more complexity.

-Andy
